subject.title: fix(hooks): wire message:sending internal hook to user-defined hooks

question: Should workspace `message:sending` hooks observe the final post-policy message, or intentionally receive pre-policy content even when a plugin later rewrites or cancels delivery?
rationale: The choice defines a persistent hook and outbound-content security contract; code inspection can identify the inconsistency but cannot safely choose the intended observer boundary.

options.title: Post-policy observer
options.body: Emit the internal event after the modifying plugin hook succeeds, using the final content and skipping cancelled messages.

options.title: Explicit pre-policy audit event
options.body: Keep pre-policy observation only under a distinct documented event contract that cannot be confused with the message actually being sent.

options.title: Defer for unified design
options.body: Pause this branch and resolve internal and plugin hook ordering through the broader exactly-once delivery design.

recommendation.title: Post-policy observer
recommendation.body: Emit the internal event after the modifying plugin hook succeeds, using the final content and skipping cancelled messages.

likelyOwner.reason: The related maintainer-associated PR already defines exactly-once `message_sending` ownership and ordering across delivery paths.
